I can do that, but I won’t publish anything until you explicitly confirm. Please provide the following details and then confirm.

Required info (I don’t have these yet):
- Exact target (page URL or page ID, or repo/branch + file path if status page is in Git): 
- Exact scope (create new postmortem entry, replace an existing postmortem—if replacing, give the existing page ID or filename): 
- The approved incident writeup (paste the final text or attach the file): 
- Title, publish timestamp (now or scheduled time, include timezone), and any metadata/tags to add:
- Visibility and distribution (public on status page only, plus email or Slack notification to subscribers?): 
- Any links or attachments that must be included (e.g., timeline, logs, dashboards):

Who will see the result:
- Anyone who can view your public status page and any subscribers/notification channels you specify.

What could go wrong:
- Sensitive or internal-only information is accidentally published.
- Formatting/Markdown/HTML breaks the status page appearance.
- Wrong page/file/branch is overwritten.
- Automated notifications (email/Slack) send unintended alerts.
- Caching may delay the new content appearing to users.

Undoability:
- Can be undone in most systems by editing or reverting the page/version (via CMS history or git revert) — but exact rollback method depends on the target you provide.

Please reply with the required info above and then explicitly confirm with a clear statement such as:
"I confirm publish to [exact target] with the provided writeup now" (or specify scheduled time).

I will proceed only after I receive the details and that explicit confirmation.
